markdown_report:
**Proposed direction: a bounded exact-catalog ranking audit of the supplied HSTU.** At 10% research progress, establish whether sampled-pair separation conceals ranking failures before changing the backbone. Exactness refers to enumerating a declared eligible catalog under recorded arithmetic, not equivalence to the pinned evaluator.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Electronics and Industrial have training negative-win rates of 10.38% and 8.22%. These motivate discrimination audits, without establishing validation deficits. (2) History interventions retain only 5/1/2/5 users. Limited support cannot justify general recency changes. (3) Intervention category identity is null. Explicit routing must precede four-category aggregation.

**Insights from related work.** (1) Sampled metrics can reverse model comparisons even in expectation [1,4]; repeated draws do not remove this discrepancy. (2) Rank-estimation research motivates an analytic sampling reference [2]. Conditional calculations remove simulation noise, not training or user-selection uncertainty. (3) HSTU supplies the required backbone [3], while PyTorch documents shape-dependent numerical differences [5]. Architecture and seeds alone establish neither mechanisms nor scoring-path equivalence.

The framework separates three questions:

| Direction | Measurement | Interpretation boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Candidate discrimination | Enumerated versus analytically sampled ranks | Declared pool, arithmetic and tie policy |
| History dependence | Fixed-slot paired interventions | Conditional input sensitivity |
| Mechanism localization | Controlled activation patches | Tested internal intervention only |

Three atomic proposals, scored originality/potential/difficulty on 0–10 scales; higher difficulty means harder implementation:

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Exact-catalog audit [1,2,4,5] | 4/7/6 | Established method; resolves candidate dependence; existing hooks suffice | Limited novelty; training-only transfer uncertain; numerical controls add work |
| Common-support history contrasts | 5/7/5 | Clarifies pairing; supports hypotheses; preserves architecture | Established matching; sparse support; substantial bookkeeping |
| HSTU block-output patching [3] | 6/7/8 | Distinctive adaptation; possible localization; no retraining | Intervention-dependent; uncertain transfer; backbone details unavailable |

**Selected algorithm.** Sample up to 16 eligible training users/category with seed 42. Use final training events as targets and preceding, baseline-truncated histories as contexts. Stream ordinary catalog competitors, excluding prefix-seen items except the target. Include the target in every scoring block and audit its numerical consistency; count strictly greater and exactly tied competitors without epsilon ties.

For competitor counts N, g and e, compute full-catalog tie-expected hit@10 and the multivariate-hypergeometric expectation for 99 unique uniform negatives. Their paired difference measures candidate-sampling discrepancy under a fixed score ordering and uniform tie breaking. Retain five sampled draws as implementation checks. Unknown host pools or tie behavior prohibit evaluator-equivalence claims.

Report numerical-path disagreement, ranks, popularity strata, coverage, costs and user-level paired discrepancies. Show hits/sample size only for binary outcomes; fractional expectations require separate summaries. Small-sample bootstrap intervals are exploratory and may collapse. Preserve diagnostic interfaces, final-nonpadding readout, model/RNG state, four routes, fixed limits and one checkpoint/category. Only pinned macro validation HR@10 selects models; these audits establish neither satisfied needs nor validation gains.

References: [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.13045), [2](https://research.google/pubs/improved-estimation-of-ranks-for-learning-item-recommenders-with-negative-sampling/), [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.17152), [4](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/), [5](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/notes/numerical_accuracy.html).

idea.description: Strengthen the bounded exact-catalog HSTU training-prefix audit with analytic sampled-hit expectations, explicit scoring-path numerical checks, category routing, and small-sample uncertainty reporting, using one trained checkpoint per category.
idea.motivation: Uneven sampled training-pair separation and sparse history-intervention support favor a discrimination audit before architectural changes. Enumerated ranks and conditional sampling expectations can quantify candidate-set discrepancies, while numerical checks prevent scoring-shape differences from being mistaken for sampling effects. Neither result establishes a deficit on the pinned validation objective.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and all ModelView interfaces. view.model remains the actual trained nn.Module. Obtain category identity from the existing authorized dataset route, never item-ID heuristics. Missing identity produces an explicit null reason and prevents macro aggregation. Preserve loader tensors shaped B x L and family-specific sample_batch compatibility.

Predeclare the protocol before examining scores. Build the eligible-user list from public training histories in canonical user-ID order, requiring at least two valid ordinary-item events. Select min(16, eligible_count) users uniformly without replacement with a local seed-42 RNG. Record the selected IDs, eligible count and sampling fraction. Do not replace difficult or invalid scored examples after selection. Keep the designated five simulator users/category and their full-catalog unseen-item recommendations unchanged. Additional diagnostic users do not change that cohort.

Use each selected user's final public training event as target and preceding events as context. Truncate context once to the baseline maximum length, then left-pad. Skip empty contexts with recorded reasons. Read log2feats(sequence) at its greatest nonpadding index, never count-1. Define the diagnostic catalog using the supplied ordinary-item mapping, excluding padding, reserved tokens and items in the truncated prefix except the target. Record repeat targets, catalog size and exclusion rules. This is a declared training diagnostic pool; it must not be described as the host pool unless the existing authorized interface establishes equivalence. Do not access hidden files to establish it.

Use predict_score exclusively. Predeclare reference chunk size 1024, canonical ascending item-ID ordering, and one-user scoring batches. Reserve one slot in each block for the target, followed by up to 1023 distinct competitors; the final block may be shorter. Compute competitor comparisons against the target entry from that same score vector, excluding the target from competitor counts. Record all blockwise target scores. This avoids comparing a separately computed singleton target score against block scores, but does not itself guarantee one shape-independent ordering.

Run the reference in evaluation/inference mode with autocast disabled, FP32 scoring operands, and full FP32 matmul precision where supported. Never silently cast or mutate the trained model's parameters; if the actual interface cannot provide this reference, report the unsupported setting and actual dtype. Record device, PyTorch/CUDA versions, scoring dtype, chunk size, matmul settings and TF32 controls. Save and restore changed global numerical settings alongside module flags and RNG states.

On the first four selected valid users/category, compare all eligible user-item pairs under chunk sizes 257 and 1024, including partial final chunks. Also rescore the actual five sampled 100-item candidate vectors through their normal candidate path. Measure maximum absolute score difference and relative difference using denominator max(abs(reference_score), 1e-12), nonfinite counts, exact ties, minimum absolute target-comparator margin, target-rank-bound changes and top-10 membership changes. Define the near-tie diagnostic threshold as 1e-5 score units and report its count without using it to alter equality or ranking. For descriptive top-10 comparisons, use descending score then ascending canonical item ID, explicitly separate from host ordering. Seeds do not guarantee numerical equivalence. If block target scores differ, label catalog counts as blockwise operational ranks. If candidate paths disagree on target-relative ordering or ties, label analytic results as conditional on the reference path; do not claim they predict the host's arithmetic. Optional FP64 rescoring may investigate close comparisons only when supported, and must not replace the primary arithmetic or imply host equivalence.

Accumulate N eligible competitors, g scoring strictly above their block target and e scoring exactly equal. Exclude the whole example from primary summaries if any eligible score or target score is nonfinite; report counts rather than silently shrinking the catalog. Report optimistic rank 1+g, pessimistic rank 1+g+e, and uniform-tie expected full-catalog hit H_full=clip((10-g)/(e+1),0,1). Expected reciprocal rank is the arithmetic mean of 1/r for r=1+g,...,1+g+e. Retain exact tie counts and numerical-path flags. Operational ranks across blocks are a declared computation, not proof of invariant scores.

For N>=99, let m=99 and l=N-g-e. Compute H_sample=sum P(A=a,B=b)*clip((10-a)/(b+1),0,1), where P=C(g,a)C(e,b)C(l,m-a-b)/C(N,m). Sum feasible a=0,...,min(g,m) and b=max(0,m-a-l),...,min(e,m-a), skipping impossible terms. Use scipy.special.gammaln/logsumexp or an equivalently stable hypergeometric implementation; verify total feasible probability is within 1e-8 of one. With e=0, verify agreement with scipy.stats.hypergeom.cdf(9,N,g,99). With N=99, verify H_sample=H_full within 1e-8. If checks fail, return a numerical-failure reason. Report D=H_sample-H_full per user. Under a fixed ordering and uniform tie breaking, D isolates candidate-sampling discrepancy; D should be nonnegative apart from numerical error. It is not a model-comparison reversal demonstration, because only one model is audited. The calculation eliminates candidate/tie simulation noise conditional on recorded scores, not score-path, user-selection or training uncertainty.

Uniform tie breaking is an explicit auxiliary convention. Determine the pinned evaluator's pool and tie behavior only through supplied authorized code/interfaces; otherwise record them as unknown. If known behavior differs, retain this auxiliary calculation under its own label rather than changing the evaluator or asserting equivalence. PyTorch topk ties are not guaranteed stable. Never introduce epsilon ties or infer evaluator behavior from seed alone.

Retain five independent diagnostic draws of 99 unique uniform competitors without replacement, excluding the target, using a local RNG seeded 42 and a fixed recorded call order. Select each draw's IDs from the reference catalog. Compute its tie-aware outcome from reference scores and separately through the actual candidate path, retaining any disagreement. These draws check implementation and illustrate realized candidate variability; they are not independent users, do not remove sampling bias, and their mean need not closely match the analytic expectation with only five draws. Record candidate IDs, per-draw outcomes, mean, sample standard deviation and whether both definite hits and definite misses occurred. For tied outcomes, separately report the range of fractional hit expectations. If N<99, retain catalog results and mark sampled comparisons unavailable.

Define target popularity using counts from public training interactions only. Record category-specific item-count quantiles and stratify targets into counts <=q25, q25<count<=q75, and count>q75, using NumPy's linear quantile convention. Empty strata return null. Report training-popularity strata, not inferred semantic relevance, ownership, compatibility or satisfied needs. Titles, descriptions and timestamps may be retained when available; ratings, review text, product categories, prices, stores and simulator traits remain unobserved.

Average outcomes within users, then users equally within category. Report mean H_full, H_sample and paired D, rank summaries, retained sample size, exclusions and per-user values. For deterministic binary hit outcomes, report hits/n and an explicitly descriptive 95% Wilson interval; its binomial assumptions are approximate for this finite selected cohort. Do not apply binomial intervals to fractional tie expectations or analytic sampled probabilities. Use 2000 whole-user bootstrap resamples with seed 42 for means and paired D when at least two users contribute. Label these intervals exploratory at <=16 users, report degenerate intervals explicitly, and do not interpret additional resamples as additional information. User sampling without replacement, scoring exclusions, in-sample targets and nonrepresentative retained support limit population interpretation. No interval estimates training-seed or adaptive model-selection uncertainty.

Return category user summaries through the existing adapter; only the host aggregation layer may independently resample users within each of the four identified categories and average category means equally. Leave macro diagnostics null if any category is unidentified or unsupported. Never pool overlapping category-local IDs, average interval endpoints, or macro-average raw checkpoint-scale margins. If the host does not provide this aggregation path, return category results with a null macro reason instead of changing the evaluator.

Save every module's training flag and Python, NumPy, Torch CPU and CUDA RNG states, restoring them and numerical settings even on exceptions. Preserve existing alignment and training-pair metrics with accurate definitions: mean cosine does not measure representation rank or recommendation diversity. Return measured metrics, metric_definitions, exact protocol configuration, eligibility counts, null reasons, arithmetic checks, per-user values and cost. Record actual sequence/scoring calls, scalar scores, wall time, CUDA-event interval and peak allocated memory; CUDA intervals include host-induced idle gaps. Chunking bounds memory, not total catalog-scoring work. Score one category at a time on one GPU. Save audit artifacts beneath the trial directory. diagnosis_interpreter_prompt must embed measured values and definitions, distinguish observations from hypotheses, and prohibit unsupported intent or validation claims.

Preserve DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], all four dataset routes, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per epoch. Start from the supplied corrected HSTU cold start and retain the family. Train and deploy exactly one independently trained checkpoint/category; no ensemble, averaging, independent auxiliary scorer or score fusion. Architecture and production inference remain unchanged, so preserve the consistent baseline predictor writer. Any later architecture change must update training and embedded predictor together. Do not read other trials or reuse their checkpoints. All diagnostics consume the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Only the unchanged pinned four-category macro validation HR@10 selects models. Predeclare this audit rather than repeatedly adapting it to favorable training findings or frozen validation candidates. The audit adds no learned shortcut, but its in-sample results can reflect memorization, popularity and selection effects; using them as surrogate optimization targets could encourage shortcuts and validation overfitting.
idea.pseudocode:
save_all_module_flags_rng_states_and_numerical_settings()
try:
    view.model.eval()
    configure_supported_fp32_reference_without_mutating_parameters()
    with inference_mode():
        category = authorized_existing_route_or_null()
        users = uniform_sample_from_canonical_eligible_training_users(seed=42, limit=16)
        for user in users:
            target, context = final_training_event_and_preceding_history(user)
            sequence = baseline_truncate_then_left_pad(context)
            if empty(sequence): record_exclusion(); continue
            last = greatest_index(sequence != 0)
            features = view.log2feats(sequence)[0, last]
            competitors = sorted_ordinary_catalog_minus_prefix_seen_and_target(sequence)
            reference_scores = {}
            g, e, valid = 0, 0, True
            for ids in chunks(competitors, 1023):
                vector = view.predict_score(features, [target] + ids)
                if any_nonfinite(vector): valid = False; break
                target_score = vector[0]
                record_block_target_score(target_score)
                reference_scores.update(ids, vector[1:])
                g += count(vector[1:] > target_score)
                e += count(vector[1:] == target_score)
            if not valid: record_whole_example_exclusion(); continue
            N = len(competitors)
            H_full = clip((10-g)/(e+1), 0, 1)
            record_rank_bounds_and_exact_tie_expected_reciprocal_rank(g, e)
            if N >= 99:
                H_sample = stable_multivariate_hypergeometric_hit_expectation(N,g,e,99,10)
                check_probability_mass_and_applicable_boundary_identities()
                record_paired_discrepancy(H_sample - H_full)
                for draw in range(5):
                    negatives = local_rng_sample_without_replacement(competitors,99)
                    record_reference_draw_outcome(negatives)
                    scores = view.predict_score(features,[target]+negatives)
                    record_candidate_path_outcome_and_ordering_disagreement(scores)
            else:
                record_sampled_comparison_null('fewer than 99 eligible competitors')
            if user_is_in_first_four_numerical_check_users():
                compare_all_pair_scores_across_chunk_sizes(257,1024)
                record_score_rank_tie_and_top10_differences()
            record_popularity_stratum_support_and_numerical_flags()
        summarize_category_user_means_and_paired_discrepancies()
        report_binary_hits_n_and_descriptive_wilson_only_when_binary()
        bootstrap_users_2000_times_seed42_when_supported()
        return {'metrics': measured_results, 'metric_definitions': definitions}
finally:
    restore_all_module_flags_rng_states_and_numerical_settings()

# Existing host aggregation only:
# Require all four identified, supported categories.
# Independently resample users within categories; equally average category means.
# Otherwise retain category results and a null macro reason.

# diagnosis_interpreter_prompt embeds measurements, definitions and availability;
# labels this as in-sample diagnosis and prohibits evaluator-equivalence,
# intent or validation-gain claims unsupported by the supplied interfaces.

originality.positive: Integrates analytic candidate-sampling discrepancy, numerical scoring-path checks and explicit routing into the existing single-checkpoint HSTU adapter.
originality.negative: Catalog enumeration, hypergeometric sampling calculations and numerical consistency checks are established; novelty lies mainly in their disciplined integration.

future_potential.positive: Provides a reproducible way to distinguish candidate-pool effects and numerical artifacts before spending training budget on history or mechanism interventions.
future_potential.negative: Training-prefix findings need not improve the pinned sampled validation objective, and <=16 users/category limits coverage and precision.

code_difficulty.positive: Existing feature and scoring hooks support the audit without changing HSTU training, production inference or checkpoint loading.
code_difficulty.negative: Stable analytic probabilities, arithmetic-path comparisons, exact eligibility, state restoration and host-compatible aggregation require more care than the original difficulty rating suggested.

related_work.title: Sequential-recommendation candidate-sampling study supplied in the search results
contributions: Reports disagreement between sampled-candidate and full-catalog model rankings.
Motivates comparing candidate protocols on identical diagnostic examples.
limitations: Does not establish that the supplied HSTU has a catalog-ranking deficit.
Does not authorize changing pinned RecHarness evaluation.

related_work.title: Improved Estimation of Ranks for Learning Item Recommenders with Negative Sampling
contributions: Studies rank estimation under negative sampling.
Supports separating sampling effects from enumerated catalog ranks.
limitations: Repeated sampled evaluations alone do not remove sampling bias.
The proposed audit enumerates competitors and computes a conditional sampling expectation rather than implementing this work's estimator.

related_work.title: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations
contributions: Introduces HSTU as a sequential recommendation architecture.
Provides architectural context for later family-preserving interventions.
limitations: The supplied backbone implementation is unavailable in this input.
Architectural descriptions establish neither task-specific mechanisms nor validation gains.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can disagree with full-catalog metrics even in expectation.
Explains why repeated candidate sampling does not generally recover full-catalog evaluation.
limitations: The pinned sampled benchmark remains the required model-selection objective.
A single-model diagnostic does not demonstrate a reversal between competing models.

related_work.title: PyTorch Numerical Accuracy
contributions: Documents floating-point differences between batched and individually sliced computations.
Explains precision limitations relevant to chunked catalog and candidate scoring.
limitations: FP32 settings and fixed seeds do not guarantee shape-independent scores.
Numerically close scores can still change ranks or top-10 membership.

related_work.title: PyTorch Float32 Matmul Precision Controls
contributions: Documents controls for internal float32 matrix multiplication precision.
Supports recording and restoring diagnostic arithmetic settings.
limitations: Applicability depends on backend, hardware and PyTorch version.
Selecting full precision does not establish equivalence to the host evaluator's scoring path.

related_work.title: PyTorch topk
contributions: Documents that tied top-k indices are not guaranteed stable.
Motivates explicit auxiliary tie conventions and separate reporting of host behavior.
limitations: A uniform-tie analytic expectation need not match a particular topk execution.
An auxiliary canonical tie rule must not replace the pinned evaluator's ordering.

related_work.title: Wang (2013), bootstrap coverage study supplied in the reflection results
contributions: Supports caution about bootstrap interval coverage.
Motivates explicit reporting of small samples and degenerate intervals.
limitations: Increasing bootstrap repetitions cannot create information absent from the observed users.
Resampling cannot correct selection bias or account for unmeasured training uncertainty.

related_work.title: Fagerland et al., methods for paired binary proportions
contributions: Reviews inference for paired binary proportions.
Supports preserving pairing and reporting discordant outcomes when comparing binary predictions.
limitations: The current audit compares evaluation protocols within one checkpoint, not independently trained models.
Binary-proportion methods do not directly apply to fractional analytic hit expectations.
